title: Izzy
content: Having general anesthesia in the past with no complications, the anesthesiologist gave me Percocet and then handed my case over to the CRNA. For unknown reasons at the time, the CRNA gave me Versed, fentanyl, and then Dilaudid in the wrong dosage, miscalculating my body weight in kilograms. I woke up much later after surgery. I found out later that they had to do resuscitation efforts, including Narcan and other measures to revive me. I spoke to the post-op nurse about it, and she became emotional. The anesthesiologist, whom I’d never met before, confirmed the overdose and apologized six months later. I had an experience during this time. I encountered a definite being, or a voice clearly of mystical or unearthly origin. I felt the presence of God, and also felt like I was a part of Him. I felt the presence of my brother and loved ones who had passed, but the conversations were nonverbal.

elements.At the time of your experience, was ther: Yes, Surgery-related, Drug or medication overdose, While under general anesthesia, Clinical death (cessation of breathing or heart function)
elements.Did you feel separated from your body?: I clearly left my body and existed outside it
elements.How did your highest level of consciousn: More consciousness and alertness than normal, I feel it mostly in my gut.
elements.At what time during the experience were: During general anesthesia, there was no recollection whatsoever. At a subconscious level, everything changed. I woke up after resuscitation with a totally different view on my brother’s death that occurred in 2004, and other loved ones who had passed away.
elements.Did time seem to speed up or slow down?: Everything seemed to be happening at once; or time stopped or lost all meaning, Time and space felt negotiable
elements.Please compare your vision during the ex: I still experience colors and sounds a lot more intensely than before my experience. Two years after my experience, I took medication for anxiety. By reducing anxiety, I experienced life even more. I felt music deeply and was more present in my body. Anxiety related to my experience was due to the CRNA overdosing me. I am now finally processing my experience, that was helped along with the medication.
elements.Please compare your hearing during the e: I can still intensely hear and am sometimes overwhelmed by some sounds.
elements.Did you seem to be aware of things going: Yes, and the facts have been checked out
elements.Did you encounter or become aware of any: Yes, My brother, who passed away 18 years prior.
elements.Did you see, or feel surrounded by, a br: A light clearly of mystical or other-worldly origin
elements.Did you see an unearthly light?: Yes, I cannot describe it in words because I was part of the light.
elements.Did you seem to enter some other, uneart: A clearly mystical or unearthly realm, I was part of the light and love
elements.What emotions did you feel during the ex: God equals love, joy, peace, kindness, mercy, smiles, forgiveness, deep knowledge and understanding of many things in past, present, and future.
elements.Did you feel a sense of harmony or unity: I felt no longer in conflict with nature
elements.Did you suddenly seem to understand ever: Everything about myself or others, Mostly everything about God, myself, others, and this world
elements.Did scenes from your past come back to y: I felt the past and understood much more about it.
elements.Did scenes from the future come to you?: Scenes from my personal future, Yes, and much more, not just about myself. I still dream of future scenes. The experience increased my dream experiences tenfold. Dreams about past, present, and future
elements.Did you come to a border or point of no: I came to a barrier that I was not permitted to cross; or was sent back against my will, Very unpleasant and devastating to be back in my body until I was willing to understand my purpose
elements.Have your religious practices changed si: Yes, Much closer to God's presence, less performance.
elements.Did your experience include features con: Content that was both consistent and not consistent with the beliefs you had at the time of your experience, I had to leave behind beliefs that no longer aligned with God or myself. I understood love and acceptance, but also justice and the importance of setting boundaries. I gained wisdom, courage, and mental stability.
elements.Did you have a change in your values and: Yes, I became more certain about God, the afterlife, and my brother’s passing.
elements.Did you seem to encounter a mystical bei: I encountered a definite being, or a voice clearly of mystical or unearthly origin, Feeling the presence of God, being part of Him.
elements.During your experience, did you gain inf: Yes, God, only as being part of him
elements.During your experience, did you gain spe: Yes, I gained awareness about the past, present, and future.
elements.During your experience, did you gain inf: Yes, I had to be willing to understand my purpose back on earth.
Yes, There's more life after this earthly life
elements.Did you gain information about how to li: Uncertain, It’s hard to explain. Words come as I still experience life here. In some way, the understanding I received from my experience reveals itself as life unfolds.
elements.During your experience, did you gain inf: Yes, After coming back, I found the courage to talk about the abuse I’ve experienced and heal, along with others willing to heal, including those who hurt me. I also gained the strength to fight for justice.
Yes, I felt part of love. God is love.
elements.What life changes occurred in your life: My perspective on death changed significantly after experiencing my loved ones in my experience, especially my brother.
elements.Have your relationships changed specific: Yes, I don't people-please as I used to. I've developed a voice, meaning I now speak my mind.
elements.Was the experience difficult to express: Yes, Extremely difficult, I cannot express it in words. I can feel the experience. Shock perhaps, because it is so different from this world.
elements.How accurately do you remember the exper: I do not know how my remembrance of the experience compares to my remembrance of other life events that occurred around the time of the experience, It’s based on feelings rather than conscious memory.
elements.Are there one or several parts of your e: The feeling of the experience remains within me. I'm still part of love. I cannot undo what was done. This is who I am for the rest of my life on this earth.
elements.Did you have any knowledge of near death: Yes, I woke up the morning of my surgery and felt immense fear. I prayed and it went away. I felt peace and knew I had to be in surgery and then had an experience.
elements.What did you believe about the reality o: Experience was definitely real, But I didn't really want to talk about it. I felt intense grief; most likely for being overdosed. Even after 3 years, I am just now deciding to explore it further.
elements.What do you believe about the reality of: Experience was definitely real, More acceptance than grief, finally processing and talking about it makes it all better.
elements.At any time in your life, has anything e: Yes, Yes, in dreams very often, but also my feelings are often intense, though likely not as much as during the experience, which was real life.
elements.Is there anything else that you would li: God is not abuse; God is love. Love is not abuse. Due to personal experience.
